expected_evidence: Geological: sediment/ice-core stratigraphy across multiple continents lacking a consistent, reproducible YD-boundary impact layer (no verifiable global platinum spike, shocked quartz, or spherule horizon at correct age in independently dated sections)

Geological/geochemical: failed independent replication of proposed impact markers (nanodiamonds, magnetic microspherules, iridium/platinum anomalies) by other labs, or demonstration that these markers have non-impact origins such as volcanic ash, terrestrial fungal or algal material, or cosmic dust background variability
Astronomical: absence of a corresponding impact crater or airburst structure of appropriate size and age; failure of proposed comet-fragmentation trajectory models to be corroborated

Geological/climatological: alternative causal chain evidence for YD cooling such as glacial Lake Agassiz meltwater pulse into the North Atlantic or AMOC shutdown proxies, better chronologically constrained than an impact trigger
Material/archaeological: continuity of Clovis and other Paleoindian lithic traditions across the YD boundary rather than an abrupt population collapse tied to a single catastrophic event

Genetic: absence of a sharp human or megafaunal population bottleneck signature precisely coincident with the proposed impact-winter date, or extinction timing shown to be staggered rather than instantaneous
Model-prior: published critique and consensus literature documenting non-replication and methodological problems with the original impact-hypothesis papers
response.rationale: This hypothesis is a refutation claim, testable mainly via modern re-analysis of well-preserved, precisely-dated geological and paleoclimatic archives such as ice cores, varved lake sediments, and loess sections, rather than fragile perishable materials. Geological (0.6-0.65) and astronomical (0.7) detectability for the younger-dryas and upper-paleolithic rows are comparatively high, and the real debate around this topic (failed replications of nanodiamond and platinum signals, absence of a matching crater, competing meltwater-pulse explanations) is the kind of evidence such records preserve well. Material and genetic lines (archaeological continuity, extinction/bottleneck timing) are moderately detectable (0.3-0.35) since Paleoindian sites and ancient DNA records exist but are sparse and unevenly distributed across multiple continents, weakening any globally uniform refutation claim. Textual, linguistic, oral_tradition, and iconographic channels are essentially non-viable (0.0-0.1) for this pre-literate period and are largely irrelevant to adjudicating this specific hypothesis. Because the geological and astronomical channels most relevant to this debate have relatively strong detectability, an absence of a confirmed, universally reproduced impact signature is more likely to reflect genuine non-existence supporting refutation than a mere detectability failure. I set the blended adjustment at 0.55, weighted toward the higher-detectability geological, astronomical, and model-prior channels that actually carry this debate. Note: my familiarity with the real-world Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis controversy comes from training knowledge and should be treated as unverified model-prior background rather than an established fact within this exercise.
